deepdive.co: GMR POW AND URBAN INFRA L

target.name: GMR POW AND URBAN INFRA L

bull_bear.body:
- Consolidated net debt has fallen significantly over the last four years, aided by the Hyderabad-Vijayawada settlement, divestment of a 30% stake in PT Golden Energy Mines Tbk, and the Rajahmundry OTS/Haryana Discom claim receipt.
- A framework agreement is in place to divest stakes in Bajoli Holi (79.86%), Vemagiri (51%) and Rajahmundry (51%).
- Gross debt fell INR0.8bn QoQ (Corporate -INR4.1bn, Energy -INR2.1bn) even as Smart Meter debt rose INR5.8bn to fund the AMI rollout; refinancing at Warora is targeted to mobilise cash flow and de-lever.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- GPUIL operates across four verticals - Energy (thermal, hydro, solar, wind), Smart Metering (AMI), Transportation & Urban Infra (highways, EPC, Krishnagiri SIR) and Smart Mobility (EV charging) - and is pivoting under a 'GPUIL 2.0' strategy from conventional energy toward smart metering, renewables and EV/smart-mobility adjacencies.
- Management cites nearly three decades of presence across power-generation sources, in-house project management/O&M/policy-advocacy capability, over a decade of energy-trading experience, and GMR Group synergies (airports as fleet-owner/cab-aggregator hubs) as the basis for the GPUIL 2.0 transition.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Litigation] NHAI has filed a Special Leave Petition in the Supreme Court challenging the Delhi High Court order referring the Ambala-Chandigarh toll dispute to de-novo arbitration; arbitration awaits the SLP outcome.
- [Litigation] The DFC Eastern Corridor EPC prolongation claim totals INR2,829cr, of which only INR506cr was considered as of 30-Jun-26.
- [Receivables] Overdue accounted receivables of ~INR6.8bn (Energy ~INR1.8bn, DFCC ~INR5.0bn), excluding claims under litigation.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: GPUIL positions itself as a diversified energy-to-urban-infrastructure platform transitioning from conventional power generation toward smart metering, renewables and smart-mobility adjacencies under its 'GPUIL 2.0' strategy, while steadily deleveraging.
